document_check.note: Document is Shao W, Zhu T, Xiong X, Xiong Y, Zhang Q, 'White matter abnormalities in metabolic syndrome patients with and without mild cognitive impairment: A diffusion tensor imaging study', Behavioural Brain Research 503 (2026) 116057. Cross-sectional DTI comparison of MetS-MCI (n=36), MetS-NC (n=30) and HC; it reports TBSS and ROI FA/MD differences, matching the cited result.

cited_result: Principal: whole-brain TBSS in MetS-MCI (n=36) versus MetS-NC (n=30) showed increased MD (6.02% of skeleton voxels) and radial diffusivity λ23 (4.38%), with no FA difference reported for this contrast. Secondary: the atlas-based ROI analysis found lower FA in SCR.L, EC.L and EC.R in MetS-MCI.
tool_reason: The cited result is a between-group comparison of imaging measures (MetS with MCI vs MetS with normal cognition) at a single time point.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined
domains.rationale: MetS definition, MCI and NC inclusion rules and exclusion criteria are explicit.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: The inclusion criteria for MetS-MCI group were the following: 1) complaints of memory decline; 2) MoCA scores ≤25; 3) absence of any other physical or mental disorders that can lead to cognitive impairment. The inclusion criteria for MetS-NC group were as follows: 1) no complaints of memory decline; 2) MoCA scores ≥26.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The single-hospital setting, recruitment period and detailed demographic and metabolic characteristics (Table 1) are given. The recruitment pathway (outpatient, inpatient, consecutive or not) is not stated.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: 36 MetS patients with MCI (MetS-MCI), and 30 age-, gender-, and education-matched MetS patients with normal cognition (MetS-NC) were recruited from the Tongji Hospital between February and November 2024.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (cognitive group membership within MetS) measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: Grouping used the MoCA and further standard tests administered by neurologists; MetS components were measured objectively.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Participants received a series of neuropsychological assessments, including MoCA for global cognition, Verbal Fluency Test (VFT) and Clock Drawing Test (CDT) for executive function, Auditory Verbal Learning Test (AVLT) for assessment of memory, and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) test, performed by two neurologists.

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MetS follows NCEP-ATP III with Asian modification (standard). MCI is defined by a study-specific rule: a memory complaint plus a single MoCA cut-off of 25 or below, with no education correction (about 40% of MetS-MCI had primary or no schooling) and no named consensus diagnostic framework.

signalling.question: Was the metabolic syndrome defined by standard criteria?
signalling.quote: MetS was defined according to the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (NCEP-ATP III) guidelines [18] and modified criteria for Asians [19]

signalling.question: Was MCI defined by standard consensus criteria?
signalling.quote: 1) complaints of memory decline; 2) MoCA scores ≤25; 3) absence of any other physical or mental disorders that can lead to cognitive impairment.

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education, smoking, drinking, vascular risk factors and MetS severity are identified and compared between the MetS groups.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: No significant difference was observed in age, sex distribution, education level, or smoking and drinking among the three groups. There was no significant difference in MetS scores between the MetS-MCI and MetS-NC groups.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated
domains.rationale: Groups are said to be matched on age, sex and education, but the matching method is not described and the groups are unequal in size. Education distribution differs noticeably (high school or above 22.2% vs 46.7%). The TBSS and ROI group comparisons are not stated to include covariates; covariate adjustment is described only for the correlation analyses.

signalling.question: Was matching used as a design strategy?
signalling.quote: 30 age-, gender-, and education-matched MetS patients with normal cognition (MetS-NC)

signalling.question: Were the imaging group comparisons adjusted for covariates?
signalling.quote: we performed correlation analyses to examine the associations between FA and MD values of ROIs and neuropsychological test scores in MetS patients, adjusting for age, sex, and education level.

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way
domains.rationale: DTI was acquired with one 3 T protocol (64 directions) for all participants and processed with a standard FSL/TBSS/PANDA pipeline, including eddy correction.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: DTI data was acquired using a single shot echo-planar imaging sequence (TR/TE = 8500/66.3 msec, FOV = 25.6 × 25.6 cm2, matrix size = 128 × 128, slice thickness = 2 mm, number of slices = 70, number of diffusion gradient directions = 64

signalling.question: Was processing standardised?
signalling.quote: Diffusivity maps based on MD, λ1, and λ23 were generated using the same steps outlined above.

domains.rationale: TBSS results are said to be corrected for multiple comparisons, but the method (for example permutation with TFCE) and any covariates are not named. The ROI comparisons across ICBM tracts are reported at P<0.05 with no stated correction. The power analysis was computed post hoc from the study's own ROI results.

signalling.question: Was correction for multiple comparisons applied and described for the voxelwise analysis?
signalling.quote: The TBSS results were corrected for multiple comparisons, with the significance level set at P < 0.05.

signalling.question: Was the correction method or model specified?
signalling.quote: Searched sections 2.4 and 2.6 for the correction method (TFCE, FWE, permutation count) and design matrix covariates; none stated: 'Then, FA, MD, λ1, and λ23 among MetS-MCI, MetS-NC, and HC groups were compared. P values < 0.05 were considered to be statistically significant.'

signalling.question: Was the sample-size or power justification independent of the results?
signalling.quote: Based on the quantitative ROI analysis result in our study, the analysis confirmed that the present sample size provided over 90 % power to detect significant differences at α = 0.05.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: no critical item answered No; items 4, 6 and 8 unclear)
overall_rationale: Inclusion criteria, setting and DTI measurement are sound, and confounders were identified. However, MCI rests on a single MoCA cut-off without education correction, and the claimed matching is undocumented with visible education imbalance. The voxelwise group comparison names neither its multiple-comparison method nor any covariates. No critical item is clearly No, so the review's rule gives some concerns.
